name: Bitcoin
day_summary: The hawkish FOMC scenario that this morning's brief warned about materialized — and BTC's response was more resilient than the worst-case script. Warsh delivered a dot plot with 9 of 18 members projecting 2026 rate hikes, the median year-end rate raised to 3.8%, PCE inflation forecasts raised to 3.6%, and then dropped all forward guidance: 'I can't give you any guidance on what we're going to do next.' BTC dipped roughly 1% to ~$65,300 immediately after the 2:00 PM ET release, then continued lower as the press conference ran, settling near $64,600 at the US equity close — down -1.57% from Tuesday's $65,633 close. The critical fact: the $63,500 two-day daily-close stop was NOT triggered. The $63,663 session low from early this morning held and was NOT broken by the FOMC selling. Michael Saylor's Strategy, which added 1,587 BTC earlier today, has an anchor in the $64,000 demand zone that proved its worth. Bears won the session; they did not win the stop.

decision.rationale: HOLD at low conviction. The hawkish scenario played out but the floor held — and Warsh's explicit abandonment of forward guidance ('I can't give you any guidance') reduces certainty about the hike path even with 9/18 dots pointing that way. The $65,000 re-risk trigger has now been breached for a second consecutive day, which makes it firmer resistance. The $63,500 two-day close stop has not been triggered. Strategy's 1,587 BTC buy and long-term holder absorption of 125,000 BTC in June remain the structural demand anchors. Historical pattern matters: 'BTC falls after 8 of the last 9 FOMC meetings, averaging ~11% the following week' — the real test is not today but the next 7 days. No new longs until BTC reclaims $65,000 on a daily close. Maintain $63,500 two-consecutive-close stop. A second daily close below $63,500 triggers exit of existing position.

analysis:
## The hawkish FOMC floor held — but the window is still dangerous

Bitcoin closed at **$64,600**, down -1.57% from Tuesday's $65,633 close, as the hawkish FOMC scenario from this morning's brief materialized in full: [9 of 18 FOMC members project 2026 rate hikes](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html), the median year-end dot rose to 3.8% from 3.4%, PCE inflation forecasts were raised to 3.6%, CME FedWatch now prices an 80% chance of at least one 2026 hike, and the DXY is estimated to have crossed the 100 regime trigger post-announcement. This was the exact worst-case scenario described in the morning brief — and BTC did not flush to $62K–$63K as that scenario projected. That is the first-order read: the bears got the fundamental catalyst and still couldn't break the floor.

## Technical analysis

**Trend:** BTC is below the $65,000 re-risk trigger for the second consecutive session, confirming it as resistance. The short-term trend is bearish. RSI estimated in the low-to-mid 40s (~43.85 per Barchart data) — neutral, not oversold, which means there is no technical demand signal from oversold conditions.

**Momentum:** Bearish. Negative perp funding and P/C at 0.98 indicate the market is positioned defensively. The funding rate flip (positive → negative) that happened overnight means the average levered trader has shifted to short/neutral — this removes the long-covering fuel that amplified the June 15 recovery rally.

**Volume — less clear than NVDA's:** ~$19B 24h volume is within the normal range. The session didn't see a volume spike on the FOMC flush, which is mildly constructive (no panic selling), but also no volume surge on the recoveries (no conviction buying).

**Pattern:** BTC is in a range-bound consolidation between $63,500 and $65,935 since June 13. The FOMC outcome defines the edges of this range: $65,000 is the top-of-range resistance (re-risk trigger, now confirmed twice), and $63,500–$64,000 is the bottom-of-range support shelf (max pain + Strategy demand + two-day stop). A directional break of either bound is the next meaningful price-discovery event.

**★ Strongest support — $63,500–$64,000 demand shelf:** This cluster has three independent anchors: (1) the two-day daily-close stop at $63,500 (where long-book exits activate), (2) June weekly options max pain at $64,000 (where dealer hedging creates natural buying), and (3) Strategy's corporate treasury demand established today in this zone. The convergence of these three at a $500 band is the most defensible support structure on the chart.

**★ Strongest resistance — $65,000 re-risk trigger:** The $65,000 level has now been tested from below on both June 16 and June 17. Each rejection reinforces the level as resistance. The trigger was originally established as the line between 'macro thesis intact' and 'yellow flag' — two closes below it converts it to confirmed resistance requiring a clean close above to re-establish as support.

**Invalidation of bearish read:** A close above $65,000 that holds for 24 hours upgrades the call to BUY and reopens the $67,000 path.

## What 'dropping forward guidance' means for crypto

Warsh's departure from forward guidance is the most important macro development of 2026 for risk assets. [The old Fed regime (Powell) gave explicit rate-path guidance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/warsh-kills-dot-plot-short-140439122.html) — you could bet on the dots. Warsh has now said explicitly: the dots are what 18 people think today, and I'm not committing to any of them. For BTC specifically: this means the 80% CME-priced hike probability is a market construct, not a Fed commitment. If Warsh's next press conference in August signals he is 'watching the data' (which is the Warsh posture he described), the 80% hike probability could evaporate on a single CPI print. Long-term, a Fed that refuses to guide is a Fed that is inherently more reactive — and a more reactive Fed means policy surprises in both directions, which historically benefits liquid, 24/7 hard assets like BTC as a volatility hedge.

## The 8-of-9 problem

[CoinSpeaker notes](https://www.coinspeaker.com/warsh-dot-plot-bitcoin-short-term-pain-long-term-gain/) that BTC has fallen after 8 of the last 9 FOMC meetings, averaging roughly an 11% drop in the following week. From $64,600 at -11% = ~$57,500 — which would breach the $63,500 stop and require position exit. The counter-argument: [long-term holders absorbed 125,000 BTC in June](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/06/17/live-markets-a-bitcoin-bottom-signal-flashed-as-holders-absorbed-125-000-btc-in-june) — and that LTH absorption is the structural argument for why this FOMC might be the 1-of-9 that doesn't follow the pattern. The stop exists precisely for this uncertainty: hold if the floor holds, exit if it doesn't.
